scenes.title: Who chooses the next step?
scenes.evidence: Three helpers can appear in the same chat window and work quite differently.

beats.label: A chatbot replies
beats.narration: Three helpers can appear in the same chat window and work quite differently. A simple question-and-answer chatbot reads your message and explains something it already has in writing. Think of asking a receptionist about opening hours.

visual.heading: A chatbot replies
visual.detail: A question about opening hours → a written answer.

beats.label: A workflow follows rules
beats.narration: A workflow is a recipe someone wrote for a computer. It can make choices, like sending an incomplete form back, because a person already specified what to do in each case.

visual.heading: A workflow follows rules
visual.detail: Missing field → return the form.

beats.label: An agent chooses
beats.narration: An agent is given a goal and some permitted actions. It decides what information to look up next as it learns more. Watch what each helper can do for the same shopper.

visual.heading: An agent chooses
visual.detail: The lookup result guides its next action.

scenes.title: Can Owen get free return shipping?
scenes.evidence: Owen bought a jacket and wants a smaller one.

beats.label: Owen’s question
beats.narration: Owen bought a jacket and wants a smaller one. First he asks about return shipping.

visual.heading: Owen’s question
visual.detail: First he asks about return shipping.

beats.label: What the policy says
beats.narration: Orbit’s chatbot reads the shop policy and says shipping is free on orders over seventy-five dollars. That explains the rule.

visual.heading: What the policy says
visual.detail: shipping is free on orders over seventy-five dollars.

beats.label: What we still need
beats.narration: The chatbot in this example has not opened Owen’s order, so it cannot say whether his purchase qualifies.

visual.heading: What we still need
visual.detail: it cannot say whether his purchase qualifies.

scenes.title: One returns form, two predictable routes
scenes.evidence: Owen submits the shop’s return form.

beats.label: Check required fields
beats.narration: Owen submits the shop’s return form. A workflow checks that the required fields are filled in.

visual.heading: Check required fields
visual.detail: Does the form include the order number?

beats.label: Complete form
beats.narration: A complete form goes into the returns queue.

visual.heading: Complete form
visual.detail: Forward the request to the returns queue.

beats.label: Missing order number
beats.narration: A missing order number sends the form back to Owen. This is still a workflow: both routes were written down before Owen bought his jacket.

visual.heading: Missing order number
visual.detail: Return the form to Owen for the missing detail.

motion.label: The order number sets the route

scenes.title: How a shipment triggers an email
scenes.evidence: Follow a parcel through a different fixed workflow at Orbit.

beats.label: Warehouse event
beats.narration: Follow a parcel through a different fixed workflow at Orbit. When Sam's warehouse marks an order as shipped, the orders system announces it.

visual.heading: Warehouse event
visual.detail: Order marked as shipped.

beats.label: Fill the template
beats.narration: A template fills in the customer's name, the item and the tracking number.

visual.heading: Fill the template
visual.detail: Insert name, item, and tracking number.

beats.label: Send the update
beats.narration: And the email goes out to the customer. Same three steps, every time, in the same order, with nothing to decide, so no language model is needed.

visual.heading: Send the update
visual.detail: The customer gets the tracking email.

scenes.title: Can Owen actually get a smaller jacket?
scenes.evidence: Now Owen asks whether he can actually get the smaller jacket.

beats.label: Look up his purchase
beats.narration: Now Owen asks whether he can actually get the smaller jacket. Scout must find which jacket he bought before it knows which size to check.

visual.heading: Look up his purchase
visual.detail: Which jacket and size did Owen buy?

beats.label: Size available
beats.narration: If there is stock, it can offer the exchange under the shop’s rules.

visual.heading: Size available
visual.detail: Check the shop rules and offer the exchange.

beats.label: Size sold out
beats.narration: If the size is sold out, it can explain the other choices. One customer needed a policy answer, a fixed process, and a decision based on fresh information.

visual.heading: Size sold out
visual.detail: Explain the remaining options to Owen.

motion.label: The next action depends on stock

scenes.title: When is an agent worth using?
scenes.evidence: So when should you use which?

beats.label: Known steps
beats.narration: So when should you use which? If you can write the steps down ahead of time, use a fixed workflow. A fixed sequence can be tested with the same starting records and checked against an expected result.

visual.heading: Known steps
visual.detail: Test a fixed workflow against expected results.

beats.label: Different requests
beats.narration: Reach for an agent when the steps depend on the request. Ana wants tracking, Grace wants a return, Owen wants a different size, and you can't predict the mix.

visual.heading: Different requests
visual.detail: Tracking, returns, and exchanges need different lookups.

beats.label: Set limits
beats.narration: Letting the model choose a new action can introduce extra calls, expense and opportunities for a mistake. So they need limits and testing, and that is a big part of this course.

visual.heading: Set limits
visual.detail: Extra calls can cost more and introduce errors.

motion.label: Can you write the steps in advance?

scenes.title: Try the three questions yourself
scenes.evidence: Cover the names of the three helpers and listen to Owen's questions again.

beats.label: Is the answer on a sign?
beats.narration: Could a printed sign answer Owen's shipping question? Yes. A chatbot can explain the same written rule to any shopper.

visual.heading: Is the answer on a sign?
visual.detail: One shipping policy can answer many shoppers.

beats.label: Is the rule already set?
beats.narration: What happens to a form with no order number? The workflow sends it back every time. A person already chose that route.

visual.heading: Is the rule already set?
visual.detail: A missing field always sends the form back.

beats.label: Which fact is missing?
beats.narration: Can Owen have the smaller jacket? We need his order and the stock result. When fresh evidence determines what to do next, that's the job for an agent.

visual.heading: Which fact is missing?
visual.detail: Check the jacket and stock before promising a swap.
